title: Vaibhav Global Ltd - 532156 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Vaibhav Global FY26: PBT up 41% YoY, record FCF of INR272 crore, EBITDA margin 10.8%; FY27 guidance 9-11% revenue growth and 50-100 bps margin expansion.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR935 crore (+10% YoY) with EBITDA of INR96 crore (about 10.3%) and PBT of INR64 crore (+41% YoY). For FY26, revenue was INR3,691 crore, EBITDA margin rose 140 bps to 10.8%, and free cash flow hit a record INR272 crore. In-house brands crossed 50% of B2C sales about a year ahead of plan, and Germany reached full-year EBITDA breakeven. Management guided FY27 to 9-11% revenue growth and a 50-100 bps EBITDA margin improvement, but gave no constant-currency guidance. U.S. and U.K. growth stayed weak in Q4, and the Mindful Souls write-off of about INR25 crore was a notable one-off.

financial_highlights.change: ROE includes one-time MAT credit benefit per management

financial_highlights.value: INR6 per share (incl. final INR1.5 recommended)

segments.name: U.S.
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 1% in local currency; growth driven by digital mix, proprietary brands and AI-led marketing, with an in-house jewellery casting line in the U.S. helping offset tariffs.

segments.name: U.K.
segments.commentary: Q4 headline revenue flat (-1% local currency). Ideal World grew 15% while TJC declined 7%; U.K. EBITDA margin improved 220 bps YoY.

segments.name: Germany
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 7%; Germany achieved full-year FY26 EBITDA breakeven and is expected to contribute to group profit from FY27.

segments.name: Mindful Souls
segments.commentary: Digital-first acquisition; INR25 crore write-off taken on conservative impairment testing. Management says the business is still profitable and shows cross-learning benefits; payback extended from 5 to 7 years. Positive numbers were seen in the current quarter.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: Lifestyle products are ~35% of total sales (medium-term target 50%). Lab-grown diamonds are ~11% of retail revenue at ASP around USD 250 (about 18 months old category).

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 9-11% (INR terms).
FY27 EBITDA margin expansion of 50-100 bps; gross margin and employee-cost efficiencies named as main sources, with shipping leverage unlikely this year.
Medium-term revenue growth guidance of 10-12% in INR.
Tax rate steady at around 22% for upcoming years.
Content and broadcasting spend to stay around 20% of sales; SG&A leverage not expected as TV savings are reinvested into digital.
Depreciation to be broadly similar in FY27 vs FY26 after the new U.K. lease; consolidation of 4 buildings into one expected to cut operating costs.
Digital mix target of 50% of B2C sales by end of FY27; long-term peak EBITDA margin of 15% seen as achievable but no precise timeline.
capex_capacity: In-house jewellery casting line operationalised in the U.S. during FY26, reducing tariff impact on shipments.
New U.K. premises lease signed around February 2026; existing buildings to be vacated and move completed during FY27, consolidating 4 buildings into one.
100% of manufacturing power from solar; two U.S. sites and one each in U.K. and Germany run fully on renewable energy.
Capex quantum and timing for FY27 were not discussed on the call.
demand_pricing: Volumes fell about 9-10% YoY across TV and digital per an analyst; management attributed this to higher average ticket size (lab-grown demand, higher metal prices) rather than weaker demand, and pointed to customer count, repeat rate and reach as better metrics.
Unique customers at 6.8 lakh in Q4; retention stable at ~38%; average 23 pieces purchased per customer on trailing 12 months; unique customer count fell as low-value one-off customers were dropped.
Digital ~44% of B2C sales in FY26; TV networks reached ~127 million households globally in Q4.

Management reported early-April/May trends: better digital traction in U.S. and U.K., TV audiences still stressed by inflation and higher gas and interest rates; Germany traction better than last quarter.
Elevated precious metal prices and cautious discretionary spend were cited as headwinds across core markets; tariff uncertainty persists.

qa_highlights.question: How can EBITDA margin rise back toward the 13-15% levels seen in FY22 when revenue is much larger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Germany's breakeven and digital/paid media investments weighed on margin; margin rose from 7% (FY23) to 11% (FY26). Leverage expected in HR, SG&A and shipping; peak 15% seen as achievable over time but no precise timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why not enter India, and will the company consider a buyback given the share price decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Agrawal said TV shopping never took off in India, so entry would be digital-only, to be considered after digital maturity in the Western markets. No buyback response was given on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Lifestyle 50% target versus in-house jewellery mix: are these contradictory?
qa_highlights.answer: Nitin Panwad clarified that in-house brands are 50% of B2C, of which 85% is jewellery and 15% lifestyle; the 35% lifestyle share and 50% medium-term target are for total group sales, including external and umbrella brands.

qa_highlights.question: Why are gross margins flat over three years despite digital mix shift, lab-grown and higher ASPs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said B2B sales growth (lower gross margin, no content cost) dilutes gross margin; Q4 gross margin rose ~180 bps and FY26 ~40 bps. Tariffs and metal spikes were a substantial headwind, and paid media channel margins are rising.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the 50-100 bps margin improvement come from, and what constant-currency growth to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin first, then employee cost efficiency; shipping leverage unlikely this year and SG&A not expected to leverage. No constant-currency guidance given; INR guidance used given macro and business transition.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a INR25 crore Mindful Souls write-off and what drove other expenses up ~16%?
qa_highlights.answer: Impairment reflects conservative testing as double-digit growth did not materialise; payback extended from 5 to 7 years. Other expenses rose on U.K. warehouse set-up, travel and AI technology spend, which management called temporary.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp rise in ROE and the ROU asset increase?
qa_highlights.answer: ROE was driven by PAT growth including a one-time MAT credit; normalised ROE still improves to ~15%. ROU increase is from a new U.K. premises lease signed around February 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Trends for U.S. growth and visibility from AI initiatives?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Agrawal cited AI across ad creatives, landing pages, conversion analytics and supply-chain forecasting, started about a year ago and accelerating recently. He expects U.S. and U.K. to reach double-digit growth in mid-to-long term but gave no timeline.

risks_watch: U.S. and U.K. top-line growth remained low (1% and -1% local currency in Q4); FY27 guidance depends on digital traction and Germany progress.
Tariff uncertainty in the U.S. and elevated precious metal prices pressuring discretionary demand and ticket sizes.
Mindful Souls impairment (INR25 crore) and payback extended to 7 years; further write-downs possible.
Digital marketing and AI investments may keep SG&A and content costs elevated (TV broadcasting ~20% of sales), limiting margin expansion.
Declining unique customer count (6.8 lakh) and volume trends; need to track whether quality-customer focus converts to growth.
Shipping costs may rise due to geopolitical disruption (management referenced Asian crisis and war).
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins, cash flow and Germany, but cautious and somewhat evasive on U.S./U.K. growth, constant-currency guidance and tariff outlook. Management repeatedly deflected volume declines and the unique customer decline toward quality-of-customer metrics.
key_quotes: Germany has turned EBITDA positive for the full year, and we generated our highest ever free cash flow of INR272 crores in FY '26.
So overall unique customers, we monitor based on how many quality of customers we're acquiring.
So volume may not be the right barometer for you to look at it.
